chunks: And it is narrated from Musa ibn Bakr who said:

I was in the service of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and I did not see anything reaching him except from the side of al-Mufaddal; and often I saw a man bring something, but he would not accept it from him and would say: Deliver it to al-Mufaddal.

key_terms.أَبِي الْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan, a title for Imam Musa al-Kadhim (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْمُفَضَّلِ: Al-Mufaddal, specifically al-Mufaddal al-Khuma'ini, the trusted companion
key_terms.خِدْمَة: Service, referring to serving the Imam
key_terms.مُوسَىٰ بْنِ بَكْرٍ: Musa ibn Bakr, the narrator of the hadith

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Musa al-Kadhim handle gifts and items brought to him through his companion al-Mufaddal?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the institutionalization of the Imamate’s administrative structure during the Minor Occultation, where al-Mufaddal ibn Umar served as the primary gatekeeper and financial agent. By routing gifts and offerings through him, the Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) established a precedent for the *fuqaha*’s role in managing communal resources, a concept that later evolved into the basis for *khums* and *sadaqat* collection under the Four Deputies.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 299 - It is narrated from Musa bin Bakr that he said:

I was in the company of Imam Musa Kadhim (a.s) and I never saw anything being brought for the Imam, but that it came to Mufaddal and many a times saw people bring something that the Imam did not accept; on the contrary he said: Deliver it to Mufaddal.
